BATTLESIM · EXPLORE UNKNOWNS · 2026-10-04

HUD, sound and app flow

The complete four-quadrant map: current evidence, user decisions, delegated technical choices, extracted taste and hidden seams. Open review items are explicit; this is a planning artifact, not evidence that the HUD has shipped.

Direction: a compact joined central deck for desktop mouse/keyboard play; simple routing; menu music + ambience that starts as early as permitted and shares audio lifetime with battle.

2 · Known unknowns → decision ledger

User-confirmed preferences: simple owners, dependencies when they simplify, immediate game-like flow, manual developer reloads, and no speculative lifecycle machinery. The user explicitly delegated matching technical decisions; taste, conflicting tradeoffs and unproven facts still require review. Delegation authorizes decisions for this walk, not HUD implementation.

3 · Unknown knowns → extracted preferences

Keep the controls together; leave more battlefield visible. The user chose B’s central joined deck, then requested D-like compression. This replaces the split-corner recommendation. Desktop/laptop mouse and keyboard is the intended environment; no touch redesign is implied.

Atmosphere matters. Menu sound serves both the game’s identity and audio continuity. The user chose restrained music with subtle ambience, not ambience alone.

Compression has a readability floor. Use icon-only buttons with name and shortcut tooltips on hover and keyboard focus. Move and Garrison have no dedicated buttons: ordinary right-click already carries both actions. The remaining strip shows Attack-move, Reverse, Attack ground, Fast move, Stop and Fire policy. Preserve the unit facts and their text sizes as spacing shrinks; validate richer real panel states during implementation. Fresh screenshot review found no clipping or overlap in the supplied states and clear hover/focus tooltips. The small weapon/ammo row remains a readability concern inherited from the previous mockup; real-state validation must address it. Icon meanings rely partly on the tooltips.

4 · Unknown unknowns → seam findings

The sweep covered the routing, battle/session, loading/replay, viewport/renderer, audio and panel seams listed below. It is a planning sweep of existing owners, not an exhaustive implementation audit. Focused recent history did not reveal a prior replacement router or menu-music implementation.

DECIDED

Exact URL publication is not a new battle

Evidence: apps/battle-lab/src/routes/battle.tsx:120 · apps/battle-lab/src/routes/battle.tsx:258

Why it bites: The route captures query input once, then directly replaces browser history after admission. A router keyed blindly by the whole URL may restart the admitted battle; a route never keyed at all may ignore later visits.

What changes: Separate navigation/session identity from publication of the exact share URL. Verify Play → admission, same-path new battle, Back and Forward.

DECIDED

Persistent device exposes cleanup ownership

Evidence: apps/battle-lab/src/LabViewport.tsx:1140 · packages/battle-renderer/src/frame/registry.ts · packages/renderer-core/src/gpuAllocations.ts:70

Why it bites: Viewport cleanup currently destroys the device. TypeGPU root destruction alone does not free scene resources; the existing registry is the owner.

What changes: Retain registry disposal, detach canvas/viewport listeners and compare device allocation counts against the retained baseline across menu/battle cycles.

DECIDED

A shared context must not retain battle graphs

Evidence: packages/battle-audio/src/battleAudio.ts:158 · packages/battle-audio/src/webAudioSink.ts:36 · packages/battle-audio/src/soundBank.ts:84

Why it bites: Closing the per-battle context currently tears down everything. Reusing a context while recreating mixers/reverbs can leave nodes and old loops alive.

What changes: One app audio owner; per-battle evidence/voices detach on exit. Reuse prepared buffers without carrying old combat events into a new battle.

SHARP EDGE

Fresh visits may need a gesture

Evidence: Chrome autoplay policy · MDN autoplay guide

Why it bites: Unmuted autoplay is browser-dependent. Prior engagement can allow it; a fresh visit may remain suspended. A previous click in another document is not proof.

What changes: Observe actual context state; attempt early and resume during permitted input. Test with a fresh profile and normal autoplay policy; do not promise unconditional sound on first paint.

DECIDED

Late work can steal the next screen

Evidence: web/src/battle/prepare/client.ts · apps/battle-lab/src/routes/battle.tsx:278 · apps/battle-lab/src/replayFile.tsx:150

Why it bites: Preparation has cancellation, but a resolved continuation still needs lifetime discipline. Replay import awaits file/storage work and then uses location.assign without an unmount guard.

What changes: Cancel preparation on departure. Keep navigation continuations scoped to the visit that requested them; stale completion must not alter the route or URL.

DECIDED

Appearance failures can strand loading

Evidence: apps/battle-lab/src/gameAppearances.ts:48 · apps/battle-lab/src/useBattleSession.ts:236

Why it bites: The appearance hook reports a rejected load only to console; world meshes depend on appearances, so a failed load can leave the cover waiting forever.

What changes: Propagate required-resource failure to the existing refusal surface. A warm-up failure must not make the main menu unusable.

DECIDED

HUD height has neighboring consumers

Evidence: web/src/hud.css:876 · web/src/battle/present/readouts.tsx:318 · apps/battle-lab/src/BattleView.tsx:254

Why it bites: Captions assume the old height; floating readouts avoid rectangles carrying data-occludes-readouts. Dense selection/state rows can exceed the sample.

What changes: Use actual layout for captions, preserve occlusion hooks and exercise multi-selection, long names, multiple ammo types, deployment and resupply.

SHARP EDGE

Pause and command input share Escape

Evidence: apps/battle-lab/src/PauseMenu.tsx:32 · apps/battle-lab/src/BattleView.tsx:119

Why it bites: Escape first cancels a command when input owns it; pause ignores prevented events. Closing pause resumes only a pause it owns.

What changes: Preserve event ownership and prevent battle hotkeys from leaking into menu controls. Verify focus and keyboard navigation with the actual pause menu.

OPEN

Long-lived GPU loss and real document departure

Evidence: packages/renderer-core/src/device.ts:141 · packages/battle-audio/src/battleAudio.ts:60

Why it bites: Device loss reports exist; audio handles pagehide/pageshow. Moving lifetimes changes who receives these events. Client navigation and real document departure are different.

What changes: During the spec, choose the simplest visible lost-device recovery and app teardown policy. Prove no destroyed device is reused; do not add automatic recovery loops.
